parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

parameters.name: engine_name
parameters.description:
Tool engine name (e.g. `assets`, `rfi`). Matches `Tool.engine_name`
for `provider_type` Project.

get.description:
Returns projects under a company that have a project-scoped Tool record
for the given `engine_name`, along with each project's active state and
whether the tool is active on that project.

Without filters all projects are returned regardless of status. Use
`filters[tool_active]` and `filters[project_active]` to narrow results,
or `filters[name]` to search by project name.

A tool is considered active when both `is_active` and `is_available` are
true, matching the criteria used by `Project#has_active_tool?`.

`name` is the project's display name: it's prefixed with the project
number (e.g. `"1234 - Downtown Renovation"`) when the company has
`prepend_project_number` enabled and the project has a number,
matching the format used by `GET /rest/v1.0/navigation`'s
`available_projects`. `filters[name]` and `sort=name` both take the
project number into account in that case.

Results are ordered by ascending project id by default. Use `sort` to
order by `name`, `project_active`, or `tool_active` instead.

parameters.name: filters[tool_active]
parameters.description:
Filter by tool activation status. `true` — tool active (`is_active`
and `is_available` both true). `false` — tool inactive.
Omit to return all records regardless of tool status.

parameters.name: filters[project_active]
parameters.description:
Filter by project active state. `true` — active projects only.
`false` — inactive projects only.
Omit to return all records regardless of project status.

parameters.name: filters[name]
parameters.description:
Search by project name. Matches projects whose `name` (as returned
in the response) contains the given value, case-insensitively — so
when project numbers are prepended, `4521`, `harbor`, and
`4521 - harbor` all match `"4521 - Harbor Tower"`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of fields to sort by, applied in order.
Prefix a field with `-` to sort it descending. For example,
`sort=-project_active,name` returns active projects first, then
inactive ones, alphabetically by name within each group.
Defaults to ascending project id when omitted. Supported fields:
`name`, `project_active`, `tool_active`.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

name.description:
Project display name. Prefixed with the project
number when the company has `prepend_project_number`
enabled and the project has a number.

tool_active.description:
Whether the tool is active on this project
(`is_active` and `is_available` both true).

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v2.0/companies/%7Bcompany_id%7D/project_tools/assets?page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&per_page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&filters%5Btool_active%5D=SOME_BOOLEAN_VALUE&filters%5Bproject_active%5D=SOME_BOOLEAN_VALUE&filters%5Bname%5D=renovation&sort=-project_active%2Cname")

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-changelog.description: Returns projects within a company that have a project-scoped tool for the given engine_name, including each project's display name, active state, and whether the tool is active (is_active and is_available both true, matching Project#has_active_tool?). The name is prefixed with the project number when the company has prepend_project_number enabled and the project has a number, matching GET /rest/v1.0/navigation's available_projects format. Without filters all records are returned. Optional filters[tool_active] and filters[project_active] boolean params narrow results by tool or project active state respectively, and filters[name] searches by the underlying project name (case-insensitive, partial match). Results are ordered by ascending project id by default; an optional sort param (e.g. sort=-project_active,name, for active projects first then inactive, alphabetically within each group) supports ordering by name, project_active, and/or tool_active, descending when prefixed with '-'; sort=name orders by the underlying project name.

When the company has prepend_project_number enabled, filters[name] now matches against the returned "number - name" value, so searching by the project number, the name, or the full "number - name" string all work.
